name: Klyvanta Companion
author: ahmedmahgoup94

sections.description:
Klyvanta Companion works with any block theme and needs WooCommerce. It adds:

  • Software plans in WooCommerce. Tick “Software plan” on a simple WooCommerce product and give it a plan code and a billing period (one month, one year or one-off). Link the plan in the Pricing plans block: the table then shows the WooCommerce price and a “Buy one month” or “Buy one year” button that puts the plan in the cart and opens checkout. A cart holds one plan at a time; opening the link again adds no second copy. Payment is taken once; nothing renews automatically.
  • Plan code on the order. Each order line carries the plan code and billing period, shown on order screens and emails and included in WooCommerce webhooks and the REST API, so your own app can set up the account.
  • Honest wording after payment. The order received page and the customer emails say the order is waiting for payment until it is paid, then your own sentence (by default: “Payment received. Your account details will be sent by email to the address on this order.”).
  • My account > Plans. Buyers see each plan they bought, the seats, the status, and when the paid period ends, with a link to buy another period.
  • Pricing plans block. Monthly and annual prices for each plan. Both prices stay readable without JavaScript and if the plugin is turned off.
  • Documentation links block. Links to your product documentation, each with a category and a short description.
  • Demo request form block. Shows a demo-request form created in Ninja Forms with name, work email, company and an optional message. After sending, visitors read “Request received. A person will reply by email to arrange a time.” If the form is missing, visitors see your fallback address and no success message; if the plugin itself is turned off, the page asks visitors to contact you by email.
  • Setup checklist (Settings > Klyvanta). For plans, it checks that a plan product is published, that pricing tables link only plans on sale, that a payment method is on and that new orders are emailed to you. For demo requests, it checks that the form emails each request to your address, that the wording is honest, and that a test request reached you and someone confirmed it.
  • Email failure notice. If WordPress cannot send an email, staff see a notice in the dashboard. Only the time and the error are kept.
  • Retention. Requests from the Klyvanta form that Ninja Forms stores are deleted after the number of days you set (90 by default). Other forms are not touched.
  • Two demos. A SaaS platform with per-seat plans, and an AI product and API with usage plans and a documentation hub. Each creates sample plan products in WooCommerce (category “Plans”) and links them in its pricing table; importing the other demo sets the first demo’s sample plans to draft. All demo text is labelled as sample content.

The plugin stores no demo request itself and sends nothing to Klyvanta.

Requirements

  • WooCommerce 10.9 or later (tested with 10.9.4, 11.1.2, 11.2.2 and 11.3.0). Works with WooCommerce’s order tables (HPOS) and with its block cart and checkout and the classic shortcodes.
  • Ninja Forms (free) for the demo-request form, optional. Without it the blocks still work and the form block shows your fallback address.
  • Email delivery that works on your host. The checklist’s test request shows whether it does; many hosts need an SMTP plugin.

Privacy

Plan orders are WooCommerce orders, stored and erased by WooCommerce like any other; the plugin adds the plan code and billing period to each plan line and stores no customer data itself. Demo requests are stored by Ninja Forms in your site’s database and emailed to the address you set. Klyvanta adds suggested wording to Settings > Privacy > Policy guide. Ninja Forms answers WordPress’s export and erase requests for these entries.
sections.changelog:
0.2.3

  • The settings screen’s styles load from a stylesheet through the admin enqueue, on that screen only.
  • Translations are loaded by WordPress itself; the plugin no longer calls load_plugin_textdomain().

0.2.2

  • The pricing table’s buy buttons use WooCommerce’s own add-to-cart link, which still opens checkout with one plan and adds no second copy. The plugin no longer reads the address.
  • Plan settings on a product are saved only with a valid form nonce and the right to edit that product.
  • The email failure notice appears on the Dashboard, Plugins and Klyvanta settings screens only.

0.2.1

  • Contributors and author set to the author’s WordPress.org account and name. Tested with WooCommerce 11.3. No change in behaviour.

0.2.0

  • Software plans sold through WooCommerce from the Pricing plans block: plan products, buy links to checkout, one plan per cart, plan code and period on the order line, honest next-step wording, My account > Plans, checklist items and sample plans in both demos.
  • Requires WooCommerce. Declares compatibility with order tables (HPOS) and the block cart and checkout.
  • Translations load from the plugin’s languages folder; translation template included.
  • Documentation links: the category label is no longer in capitals.

0.1.0

  • First release for local testing.
